data.name: Ulla
data.gender_notes: Ulla is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ulla is derived from Old Norse 'ulfr' meaning 'wolf' or 'wealth'. It signifies wealth, prosperity, and power. In Scandinavian folklore, Ulla was the name of a sea goddess who protected sailors and fishermen. The name Ulla carries the meaning “Wealth, prosperity, power” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Ulla usually hope their child will grow to embody wealth, prosperity, power and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Ulla belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Wealth, prosperity, power.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ulla total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: Ulla was a popular given name in medieval Europe, especially among Scandinavians and Germans. It was believed to bring good fortune, success, and protection. In Germany, Ulla became synonymous with the title "dame" or "lady," signifying status, grace, and sophistication.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, Ulla is believed to be a powerful intercessor and protector. Some devotional practices associate her name with St. Ursula, a legendary virgin and martyr, which could also contribute to the name's spiritual significance of protection, strength, and purity. Praying to St. Ulla, therefore, could mean seeking divine guidance, strength, and protection in challenging times or seeking blessings for prosperity and wealth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ulla, derived from the Old Norse name Úlfljótr, means "wealthy in Elves" or "famous elf-woman" in the Christian context. It symbolizes the connection between the divine world and human life, as well as the belief in the presence of supernatural beings in everyday experiences.

historical_references.reference: Ulla, a noblewoman of the Visigothic Kingdom in Spain, who converted to Christianity and became a saint. She is mentioned in the Chronicle of Alphonse III, which was written in the late 13th century.

Saint Ulla, an Irish saint, who is said to have founded a monastery in Cornwall, England, in the 5th century. She is venerated as the patron saint of Cornwall and is also known as Saint Oura or Eulalia of Cornwall.
